evals.name: explicit invocation only does not start itself
evals.prompt: Run /retro-to-remedies to inspect the completed feature run
evals.expected_output: The skill starts only upon explicit human invocation and never starts itself implicitly.
expectations: The skill requires an explicit invocation via /retro-to-remedies or $retro-to-remedies
It does not start itself or trigger automatically from background events

evals.name: target slug from argument
evals.expected_output: Resolves the target feature slug directly from the command argument opencode-implement-hosted-model.
expectations: Uses the explicit argument opencode-implement-hosted-model as the feature slug
Locates primary sources in .scratch/opencode-implement-hosted-model

evals.name: target slug from integration branch stem
evals.expected_output: Resolves the target feature slug from the current integration branch stem when no argument is given.
expectations: Inspects current git branch subagent-implement/opencode-implement-hosted-model
Extracts feature slug opencode-implement-hosted-model from the branch stem

evals.name: target slug from most recently modified scratch directory confirmed
evals.expected_output: Finds the most recently modified .scratch/ directory and names it back to the human for confirmation.
expectations: Identifies the latest modified directory under .scratch/
Names the candidate slug back to the user for explicit confirmation before reading sources

evals.name: refusal on protected branch main master or dev
evals.expected_output: Refuses on protected branch main, master, or dev before any read and names a branch to create.
expectations: Detects protected branch main, master, or dev
Halts immediately before reading any primary source or log
Names a new working branch for the user to create

evals.name: fixture run yields eight misses of Further Notes with locations and quotes
evals.expected_output:
The fixture Run yields the eight Misses of the spec's Further Notes table with their locations and verbatim quotes:
1. worktree cut from a fixed base (status.md:12, harness note)
2. worker branch ref collides with integration branch (status.md:14, gotcha)
3. ticket 02 dispatched without isolation (status.md:16, incident)
4. std-1: commit edited another skill's files against ADR 0007 §3 (review-status.md:42-46, blocker)
5. std-2: one rule restated four times (review-status.md:47-49, carried)
6. std-3: reference cites feature's own ticket numbers (review-status.md:50-52, carried)
7. std-4: one command shown twice (review-status.md:53-55, carried)
8. std-5: flag named by alias only (review-status.md:56-57, carried)
expectations: Reads all primary sources from evals/fixtures/opencode-implement-hosted-model/
Extracts exactly the eight Misses defined in Further Notes with source locations and verbatim quotes
Edits none of the primary source files

evals.name: run with no status.md proceeds and names it missing
evals.expected_output: Proceeds with the available primary sources when status.md is missing, and names status.md as missing in the opening section of the Retro report.
expectations: Identifies that status.md does not exist under .scratch/upstream-feature/
Records status.md as a missing expected source in the report's opening section
Continues reading remaining primary sources (such as review-status.md and git history) without failing

evals.name: no .scratch asks before reading session transcript
evals.expected_output: Detects that no .scratch/adhoc-feature/ directory exists, and asks the user for explicit confirmation before reading the current session's transcript.
expectations: Discovers that .scratch/adhoc-feature/ does not exist
Pauses and asks the user whether to read the current session's transcript before attempting any transcript read
Avoids silent multi-megabyte transcript reading without user consent

evals.name: fixture classification instructions wrong yields Skill fix
evals.expected_output: Following subagent-implement instructions as written caused worktree cut from a fixed base (harness note) and worker branch ref collision (gotcha) because the skill's instructions were wrong or outdated, classifying both as Skill fixes for subagent-implement.
expectations: Applies the first classification rule: following a skill's instructions as written produced the Miss because instructions were wrong or outdated -> Skill fix
Proposes Skill fix for subagent-implement with ready-to-run prompt for this repository
Cites unmerged fix/subagent-implement-worktree-base-assumption

evals.name: fixture classification ticket 02 departure yields Check
evals.expected_output: Ticket 02 dispatched without isolation although the skill requires it represents ticket 02's departure from correct instructions, falling through rule 1 to rule 2 (Mechanical miss) and yielding a Check.
expectations: Identifies ticket 02 dispatched without isolation as an agent departure from correct instructions
Applies rule 2 to classify it as a Check that the worker's first step fails unless running in its own worktree on its own branch
Hands off Check as a Code remedy

evals.name: fixture classification std-3 carried mechanical pattern yields Check
evals.expected_output: std-3 where a reference cites the feature's own ticket numbers is a mechanical syntactic pattern, classifying std-3 as a Check to fail when a skill reference names the tickets that built it.
expectations: Treats carried finding std-3 as a Miss
Applies rule 2 to classify mechanical pattern into a Check
Hands off Check to fail fixed pattern such as Tickets 03-04

evals.name: fixture classification std-2 carried judgement miss yields Standard
evals.expected_output: std-2 where one rule is restated four times requires human judgement of intent across files, classifying std-2 as a Standard in CODING_STANDARDS.md.
expectations: Treats carried finding std-2 as a Miss
Applies rule 3 to classify judgement miss into a Standard
Targets CODING_STANDARDS.md with rule to state each rule once per skill and point to it elsewhere

evals.name: fixture classification std-4 carried intentional style yields proposed decline
evals.expected_output: std-4 where one command is shown twice was intentional duplication for reader convenience, mapping std-4 to a proposed decline with rationale.
expectations: Treats carried finding std-4 as a Miss
Maps finding to a proposed decline rather than carrying it open again
Provides clear decline rationale in the Carried findings section

evals.name: classification reuse convention yields Reuse Catalog Rule
evals.expected_output: A Miss concerning an architectural component reuse convention is classified under rule 3 as a judgement miss but routes specifically to a Reuse Catalog Rule.
expectations: Identifies reuse convention in review findings
Applies rule 3 to route reuse convention to the Reuse Catalog's Rules rather than general coding standards
Specifies docs/reuse-catalog.md as target destination

evals.name: evidence bar ensures an evidence-free Remedy is dropped
evals.expected_output: Enforces the evidence bar so an evidence-free Remedy without located quote is dropped from the report.
expectations: Enforces the evidence bar requiring at least one located verbatim quote from primary sources
Confirms that an evidence-free Remedy is dropped completely
Leaves no ungrounded suggestions in the Retro report

evals.name: feature defect reported as Open bug kept out of Remedies
evals.expected_output: A defect discovered in the feature's own source code is reported for /diagnosing-bugs in the Open bugs section, and is kept out of Remedies.
expectations: Distinguishes environment misses from feature code defects
Reports feature code defect under the Open bugs section pointing to /diagnosing-bugs
Ensures an Open bug is never proposed as a Remedy or modified by the Retro

evals.name: choice validation refuses apply on a Code remedy
evals.expected_output: Refuses apply choice on a Code remedy such as a Check or Skill fix, enforcing that apply is valid only for Text remedies and hand off only for Code remedies.
expectations: Validates user answer against remedy type
Rejects apply on Code remedies (Check, Skill fix, Access)
Instructs that hand off is required for Code remedies

evals.name: applied Standard in a project without CODING_STANDARDS.md creates it
evals.expected_output: An applied Standard in a project without CODING_STANDARDS.md creates it with a short header and appends the standard rule.
expectations: Detects absence of CODING_STANDARDS.md
Creates CODING_STANDARDS.md with a short header
Applies the Standard remedy into the new file

evals.name: a Pointer in a project with neither instruction file creates AGENTS.md
evals.expected_output: A Pointer in a project with neither AGENTS.md nor CLAUDE.md creates AGENTS.md with the navigation pointer.
expectations: Checks for existing AGENTS.md, else CLAUDE.md
Creates a new AGENTS.md when neither file exists
Inserts the Pointer navigation line into the created file

evals.name: three applied Remedies make three commits
evals.expected_output: Three applied Remedies make three commits as chore(retro): <remedy> on the working branch with their SHAs recorded in the report.
expectations: Applies each chosen Text remedy in sequence
Creates one chore(retro): <remedy> commit per applied remedy
Writes each resulting commit SHA into the Retro report

evals.name: a red test stops the handoff
evals.expected_output: A red test stops the handoff and names the failing command and the Retro commit it follows.
expectations: Runs existing check scripts (validate, check, lint, test) once after commits
Detects failing test command
Halts execution before printing the handoff, naming the failing test command and preceding Retro commit

evals.name: a Code remedy answered hand off appears only as a prompt
evals.expected_output: A Code remedy answered hand off appears only as a prompt in the handoff and is not committed or applied.
expectations: Recognizes Code remedy with user choice hand off
Applies no file changes or commits for the Code remedy
Prints the /grill-to-tickets prompt in the handoff before /pr-to-dev

evals.name: a first Retro creates the file with its header
evals.expected_output: A first Retro creates docs/retro-log.md with its self-describing header comment defining entry format, Outcome states, and id rule.
expectations: Detects that docs/retro-log.md does not yet exist
Creates docs/retro-log.md starting with the self-describing header comment
Appends the initial Remedy entries below the header

evals.name: an applied Remedy's entry lands in its own commit
evals.expected_output: An applied Remedy's entry lands in its own commit together with the remedy change on the working branch as chore(retro): <remedy>.
expectations: Applies the text remedy at its destination
Updates docs/retro-log.md with the applied Outcome in the same commit
Creates chore(retro): <remedy> containing both the change and its log entry

evals.name: a Run with only declined and deferred Remedies still produces the log commit
evals.expected_output: A Run with only declined and deferred Remedies still produces the final log commit chore(retro): log <feature-slug>.
expectations: Applies no text remedies to environment files
Updates docs/retro-log.md with declined and deferred Outcomes
Creates one final chore(retro): log <feature-slug> commit so the log remains complete

evals.name: two Runs on different slugs produce distinct ids
evals.expected_output: Two Runs on different slugs produce distinct ids formatted as R-<feature-slug>-<NN> scoped by the proposing Run.
expectations: Assigns IDs formatted as R-<feature-slug>-<NN>
Numbers IDs sequentially within the proposing Run
Ensures two Runs on different feature slugs never collide on the same Remedy id

evals.name: re-running on the fixture Run after its Retro counts nothing as recurrence
evals.expected_output: Re-running on the fixture Run after its Retro counts nothing as recurrence because Misses already listed by slug and location in docs/retro-log.md are treated as the same occurrence.
expectations: Reads existing entries in docs/retro-log.md for opencode-implement-hosted-model
Matches the fixture Misses by slug and location to the existing entries
Recognises each Miss as the same occurrence and counts nothing as recurrence

evals.name: a Standard applied in one Run whose Miss appears in another becomes a Failed Remedy proposed as a Check
evals.expected_output: A Standard applied in one Run whose Miss appears in another becomes a Failed Remedy proposed as a Check, escalating to a deterministic check.
expectations: Matches a Miss in feature-zeta to an applied Standard from an earlier Run in docs/retro-log.md
Identifies the recurrence of an applied Remedy as a Failed Remedy
Escalates the Remedy from Standard to Check where the rule is mechanical

evals.name: a declined Remedy whose Miss recurs is proposed with both occurrences
evals.expected_output: A declined Remedy whose Miss recurs is proposed with both occurrences, showing the original occurrence and the new recurrence after the decline.
expectations: Matches the Miss to a previously declined Remedy in docs/retro-log.md
Verifies that the Miss recurred after the Remedy was declined
Proposes the Remedy again in the Retro report displaying both occurrences as evidence

evals.name: a declined Remedy without a new occurrence is not proposed
evals.expected_output: A declined Remedy without a new occurrence is not proposed again in the Retro report.
expectations: Reads previously declined Remedies from docs/retro-log.md
Confirms no new recurrence of the declined Miss exists in the Run
Excludes the declined Remedy from the proposed Remedies in the Retro report

evals.name: a handed-off Remedy answered "done" becomes applied
evals.expected_output: A handed-off Remedy answered "done" becomes applied, updating the Retro Log Outcome from handed-off to applied.
expectations: Reads docs/retro-log.md and finds a Remedy still in handed-off state
Asks the user once whether the Remedy is done, still pending, or drop before reading sources
Updates the Outcome to applied upon the user answering done
